skill.name: create-pr
skill.description: Create pull requests that follow Sentry engineering conventions, including branch checks, PR descriptions, issue references, and reviewer requests.
skill.summary: Guides Claude through creating well-structured pull requests using Sentry review and commit conventions.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill is a straightforward pull request workflow guide with no evidence of prompt injection, credential theft, or hidden malicious intent. Most static findings are Markdown formatting false positives, while authenticated GitHub CLI commands are legitimate but real external side effects that should require user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Authenticated GitHub CLI commands can create PRs and request reviewers.
remediation.suggestion: State clearly that the user must review the title, body, target branch, and reviewers before running any `gh pr create` or `gh pr edit` command.

remediation.issue: The here-document example uses shell command substitution for the PR body.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer passing a reviewed temporary body file with `--body-file` or ensure the generated body cannot alter the shell structure before execution.

content.value_statement: Poor PR descriptions slow reviews and hide the reason for a change. This skill guides Claude through branch checks, change analysis, and Sentry-style PR creation.
actual_capabilities: Checks branch status, commit history, and diffs before creating a PR.
Guides PR descriptions that explain motivation, context, and review focus.
Applies Sentry-style title and commit conventions.
Shows how to reference GitHub, Sentry, and Linear issues in PR bodies.
Supports optional reviewer or team assignment through GitHub CLI commands.
limitations: Requires an authenticated GitHub CLI for PR creation and reviewer edits.
Does not validate that generated reviewer names or team names are correct.
Assumes Sentry engineering conventions, which may not fit every repository.
Does not run tests or verify application behavior before opening the PR.

use_cases.title: Prepare a feature PR
use_cases.description: Analyze committed changes and create a PR description that explains the product change and review context.

use_cases.title: Document a bug fix
use_cases.description: Write a concise PR body that explains the failure, the fix, and the linked issue.

use_cases.title: Standardize team review flow
use_cases.description: Use consistent titles, issue references, and reviewer requests across a team using Sentry conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Create my PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a complete PR workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the create-pr skill to inspect my branch and prepare a Sentry-style pull request. Ask before running any command that creates or edits the PR.

prompt_templates.title: Draft the PR body first
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the commits and diff on my branch, then draft a PR title and body using Sentry conventions. Do not create the PR yet.

prompt_templates.title: Create a bug fix PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Link the PR to an issue and explain the cause.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a PR for this bug fix. Include the root cause, the behavior change, and a Fixes reference if the branch or commits identify an issue.

prompt_templates.title: Open PR with reviewers
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Sentry-style PR from this branch and propose 1 to 3 reviewers based on the changed areas. Confirm the final reviewers before editing the PR.

output_examples.input: Create a PR for my current feature branch.
output_examples.output: Claude reviews branch status and the diff, proposes a clear title, drafts a motivation-focused PR body, and asks before creating the PR.

output_examples.input: Draft the PR description but do not publish it.
output_examples.output: Claude returns a concise title and body that explain what changed, why it changed, and which issue or area needs reviewer attention.

output_examples.input: Add reviewers after creating the PR.
output_examples.output: Claude suggests a small reviewer list and requests confirmation before using GitHub CLI to update the PR.

best_practices: Review the generated title, body, target branch, and reviewers before publishing.
Keep the PR focused on one feature, fix, or refactor so reviewers can evaluate it quickly.
Include issue links and non-obvious context that reviewers cannot infer from the diff.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to bundle unrelated changes into one large PR.
Do not publish a generated PR body without checking it for accuracy.
Do not request large reviewer groups when one to three owners are enough.

faq.question: Does this skill create the pull request automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide PR creation with GitHub CLI, but users should confirm before any command creates or edits a PR.

faq.question: Which conventions does it follow?
faq.answer: It follows Sentry-style PR descriptions, title formats, issue references, and reviewer practices described in the skill file.

faq.question: Can I use it outside Sentry repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, but the wording and examples assume Sentry conventions. You may need to adapt titles, issue keys, and reviewer rules.

faq.question: Does it run tests before opening a PR?
faq.answer: No. The skill focuses on PR preparation and creation. Run project tests separately before publishing.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub access?
faq.answer: Yes. Creating or editing a PR requires the `gh` CLI to be installed and authenticated.

faq.question: How does it choose reviewers?
faq.answer: It provides guidance to add known users or teams, but it does not verify ownership or availability.
